newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel army, Arabs clash after West Bank funeral.
newsitem.headline: Israel army, Arabs clash after West Bank funeral.

text.p: Palestinians hurled firebombs and stones at Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Bethlehem following the funeral on Wednesday of an activist of the militant Islamic Hamas movement, witnesses said.

Prior to the outbreak of the unrest hundreds of Hamas supporters held a funeral procession for activist Issa Khalil Shouka, 41, killed on Monday when a bomb he was assembling exploded in his hands, Palestinian sources said.
Marchers calling for revenge against Israel draped Shouka's body in the green Hamas flag as the procession wound through Bethlehem's Manger Square, traditional birthplace of Jesus.

After Shouka's burial in nearby Beit Shahour village, Palestinians threw stones at Israeli troops, who responded with tear gas when three petrol bombs were hurled at them. No injuries were reported in the clashes.
In Ramallah on Wednesday a Palestinian youth shot in the head by Israeli troops during a West Bank clash this week died of his wounds.
Some 2,000 mourners attended the youth's funeral later in the day in his home village of Seir, near the West Bank flashpoint of Hebron.
"Ashraf Abdel Rahman Matour, 16 years old, died from a bullet in the head today," Samer Anabtawi, administrative director of Ramallah hospital, told Reuters.
Matour was critically wounded when stone-throwing Palestinians clashed with Israeli troops on Monday in the West Bank village of Beit Sahour near PLO-ruled Bethlehem.

Mourners at Matour's funeral carried Palestinian flags and chanted his name, pledging to "carry on the struggle", witnesses said. Among the mourners were senior officers in the PLO-led Palestinian security forces.
The West Bank and Gaza have been tense since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem four months ago.
The settlement work plunged Israeli-PLO peace talks into crisis, and impaired cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian security forces.
Sporadic violence has flared for weeks in Hebron, where last month a Jewish woman kindled Moslem Arab rage by putting up posters depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
